messages.author: 32bf4f27a31a68db
messages.subject: How to center coefficients?
parts:
Hi,

I'm building a hierarchical model that is essentially a mixed effects model.  (Groups of students by campus)  I thought it would be nice for interpretability to have the campus effect centered.  (They have a gaussian prior).

Stan is complaining when I try to center the vector of campus coefficients.  What am I doing wrong?

The error I get is:
     attempt to assign variable in wrong block. left-hand-side variable origin=parameter

From the line:
      theta_cent[j] <- theta[j] - theta_mean;

stan_code <- '
data {
    int<lower=0> N;
    int <lower=0> J;
    int Y[N];
    int campus[N];
    matrix[N,28] X;

}
parameters {
    vector[28] betas;
    vector[J] theta;
    real<lower=0> sigma;
    real<lower=0> tau;
}
transformed parameters {
    vector[N] Xbeta;
    real theta_mean;

    theta_mean <- mean(theta);
    for (j in 1:J){
        theta[j] <- theta[j] - theta_mean;
    }    

    for(i in 1:N){
        Xbeta[i] <-  theta[campus[i]] + X[i] * betas;
    }

}
model{
    sigma ~ gamma(0.01, 0.01);
    tau ~ gamma(0.01,0.01);
    betas ~ normal(0, sigma);

    for (j in 1:J){
        theta[j] ~ normal(0, tau);
    }

    Y ~ poisson(Xbeta);

}
'

messages.author: 6b3b475e6af83898
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to center coefficients?
parts:
As written, you don’t have theta_cent in the code below. I think if you declare a transformed parameter theta_cent and assign it the way you describe, it should work. Better to vectorize by having it be theta_cent <- theta-theta_mean; and similarly in the model section: theta ~ normal(0,tau);

OTOH, I don’t think you need to do that centering in Stan, since you’re drawing from a distribution with mean = 0. If you think the mean isn’t 0, I’d think you should model mu_theta explicitly.

Your suggestion about not centering makes sense.  I guess it isn't needed in this case.

the model runs fine without the centering part.  BUT, I see no real variance in the samples for sigma and tau.  Maybe the step size is too small, but I don't know how or why to control that.


Thoughts?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to center coefficients?
parts:
On May 20, 2014, at 11:26 PM, Joshua Rosenau <josh.r...@gmail.com> wrote:

> As written, you don’t have theta_cent in the code below. I think if you declare a transformed parameter theta_cent and assign it the way you describe, it should work. Better to vectorize by having it be theta_cent <- theta-theta_mean; and similarly in the model section: theta ~ normal(0,tau);
>
> OTOH, I don’t think you need to do that centering in Stan, since you’re drawing from a distribution with mean = 0. If you think the mean isn’t 0, I’d think you should model mu_theta explicitly.

Right. Having the prior will identify things. Not just
in Stan, but in the posterior itself. But the prior needs
to be relatively strong for this to work. If you use
a normal(0,1000) as some modelers are prone to do, that
identification is in theory only.

If you need the centering to identify the model,
then you want to reparameterize because having the unconstrained
coefficients be unidentified is bad news for MCMC.

As Michael Betancourt keeps saying, HMC is much better at exposing
the pathologies of such models in finite time than Gibbs
or Metropolis, where you can sometimes get away with it.

See the "problematic posteriors" chapter of the manual
for some examples of the kinds of priors you need for identification
and what goes wrong when you don't have them.

- Bob
